title: Choosing between int and Integer overloads
answer: For a primitive `int` argument, the `int` overload is an exact match; for an `Integer` expression, the `Integer` overload is an exact reference-type match. Java does not randomly choose between them. A null literal cannot be passed to `int`, so with only these two overloads it selects the `Integer` overload. AeroTopo's two `LanguageLab.join` methods provide this exact primitive-versus-wrapper overload pair.
